message.content: {"caption":"A boxed main-agent prompt outlining how to delegate and coordinate work among sub-agents.","description":"A rounded rectangular text panel with a dark teal header labeled “Main Agent Prompt” and a light gray body containing monospaced instructions. The prompt tells the main agent to orchestrate sub-agents to solve a supplied problem, relay the problem accurately and completely, and delegate it to as many agents as needed. It says sub-agents can access the problem statement, so long statements need not be repeated verbatim; instead, give clear direction and let them refer to it. It also explains that file and directory tools are provided to help the main agent understand the context and choose which sub-agent to call, while the main agent itself is a router and coordinator rather than the worker performing substantive tasks. Sub-agents are responsible for making the necessary state changes. There are no arrows, marks, or other graphic components.","figure_type":"other","chart_values":[]}
